content:
Tomislav Mesarić
Zagreb, Croatia | +385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com

PROFESSIONAL PROFILE
Butcher and meat-counter professional with experience since 2015 in carcass breakdown, boning, trimming, portioning and customer service. Experienced with beef, pork and lamb, fresh sausage production, FIFO stock rotation, and HACCP temperature and hygiene checks. Known for practical product advice and careful, safe counter routines.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante, Zagreb | 2019–present
- Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides per week; bone, trim and portion meat for the counter.
- Produce approximately 40 kg of fresh sausage per week during the busy season, using the shop’s recipes and processes.
- Developed the shop’s lamb merguez recipe and adjusted its ćevapi mix to 70% beef and 30% lamb following customer feedback; the ćevapi won second place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair in 2023.
- Rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO, placing older products at the front.
- Record cold-room (0–4 °C) and display-counter temperature checks twice daily.
- Serve around 120 customers on a Saturday, advising on cuts, quantities and cooking times.
- Prepare whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting orders, including ordering, butchering, seasoning and morning delivery. Largest order: four lambs and two pigs for a 180-guest wedding in 2024.
- Kept weight-loss and temperature records during a six-week dry-ageing trial of beef ribs; the shop now sells dry-aged rib by pre-order.
- Trained two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.

Counter Assistant | Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall, Zagreb | 2015–2019
- Served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till and completed cash-up.
- Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at closing.
- Wrote a closing and cleaning checklist for the slicer, mincer, counter and floor drain after a hygiene inspection remark; it remains in use at the stall.

EDUCATION & CERTIFICATES
Vocational Certificate: Butcher (3-year programme) | Food Trades School Zagreb | 2015
HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate | 2021; renewed 2024
Preparing for the Master Butcher exam (majstorski ispit) through the Chamber of Trades; exam planned for Spring 2027.

SKILLS
Carcass breakdown (beef, pork and lamb) · Boning and trimming · Meat cutting and portioning · Fresh sausage production · Knife sharpening · Mincer and bandsaw operation · FIFO stock rotation · HACCP temperature and hygiene checks · Customer service and product advice · Cash handling

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) · English (good) · German (basic)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear headings, reverse-chronological experience, measurable workload, relevant technical skills and credible achievements. It presents the candidate as both a capable butcher and customer-facing meat-counter professional. The quantified details—weekly carcass volumes, sausage production, Saturday customer volume, temperature ranges and the 180-guest wedding order—make the experience convincing. The document is professional, concise and closely aligned with the role. No unsupported skills, qualifications or experience were detected when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, standard job titles, clear dates and relevant keywords including butcher, meat counter, carcass breakdown, boning, trimming, portioning, sausage production, FIFO, HACCP, temperature checks and customer service. It should parse reliably and has a high probability of passing AI/ATS screening for this vacancy. A minor improvement would be to use the exact phrase “HACCP temperature checks” in the experience section, rather than presenting the checks only as temperature records, to mirror the advertisement more closely. The CV appropriately does not claim forklift operation, supermarket experience, tray-sealer use or self-service packaging experience that the original information does not support.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows an excellent match for the stated requirements and role expectations. It demonstrates substantially more than the required two years at a meat counter, completed butcher training, and HACCP knowledge. It also strongly supports the role’s duties: cutting and portioning fresh meat, advising customers on cuts and preparation, rotating stock using FIFO, and recording temperature checks. The customer-service examples align well with FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” promise, while the emphasis on safe routines, hygiene, reliability and practical product advice fits the company culture. The candidate’s recipe development, dry-ageing trial and apprentice training further demonstrate pride in good work and practical skills development. The candidate does not have the nice-to-have forklift licence; this is a genuine gap rather than a CV defect. The CV also does not claim supermarket, tray-sealer or self-service packaging experience, which is appropriate because those experiences are not present in the candidate material.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT: In the Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante experience section, change “Record cold-room (0–4 °C) and display-counter temperature checks twice daily” to “Record HACCP temperature checks for the cold room (0–4 °C) and display counter twice daily.” This preserves the truthful detail while matching the job advertisement’s terminology more directly.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "advising on cuts, quantities and cooking times" — the candidate's material supports advice on cuts and cooking times, but not advising on quantities.
- "HACCP temperature and hygiene checks" — the material supports temperature logging and cleaning/sanitation routines, but does not explicitly support carrying out HACCP hygiene checks.
unsupported_claims: "advising on cuts, quantities and cooking times" — the candidate's material supports advice on cuts and cooking times, but not advising on quantities.
"HACCP temperature and hygiene checks" — the material supports temperature logging and cleaning/sanitation routines, but does not explicitly support carrying out HACCP hygiene checks.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is an exceptionally strong, clear and professional CV for the role. It presents relevant butcher and meat-counter experience in reverse chronological order, uses concise bullet points, and includes credible measurable evidence: carcass volumes, sausage production, customer volume, HACCP check frequency, and the scale of wedding orders. The profile is well targeted, while the education, HACCP certificate, skills and language sections are complete and easy to scan. The recipe development, competition result, dry-ageing trial and apprentice training provide particularly strong evidence of initiative, product knowledge and pride in good work. No material content-quality defect or unsupported claim is apparent when cross-referenced with the supplied candidate information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is excellent. The CV uses standard section headings, conventional chronology, plain text formatting, readable dates and highly relevant terms such as butcher, meat counter, carcass breakdown, boning, trimming, portioning, fresh sausage production, FIFO, HACCP, temperature checks, customer service and cash handling. It should parse reliably and has a high probability of passing AI/ATS screening for this vacancy. A very minor enhancement would be to use the exact job-ad wording "cut" and "portion" in the experience or skills section where truthful; the existing wording already substantially covers these concepts. The CV appropriately does not claim a forklift licence or supermarket/self-service packaging experience.

The document shows completed butcher training, substantially more than two years at a meat counter, HACCP knowledge, customer advice, fresh-meat cutting and portioning, FIFO rotation, temperature records, sausage production and safe counter routines. It also reflects FreshCart's priorities of knowledgeable, approachable service, reliability, hygiene and pride in good work. The candidate's preparation for the master butcher exam is a relevant positive, and it is correctly presented as preparation rather than a completed qualification. The forklift licence is a genuine gap because the candidate explicitly states they do not have one; this is only a nice-to-have and is not a document defect. The candidate also has no supermarket, self-service shelving, tray-sealer or labelling-scale experience, and the CV does not claim otherwise. These are experience gaps rather than rewriting issues.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear chronological experience, relevant quantified achievements, appropriate training, and credible operational detail. It demonstrates both technical butchery ability and customer-facing counter experience. The quantified workload, customer volume, sausage production, HACCP checks, wedding order, and award make the experience more persuasive than a generic duties-only CV. The document is professional, concise, and complete for this role. No material hallucinations or unsupported claims were identified when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, reverse-chronological employment history, conventional date ranges, and readable text that should parse well in most ATS systems. It includes strong matching keywords such as carcass breakdown, boning, trimming, portioning, fresh sausage production, FIFO, HACCP, temperature checks, customer service, and cash handling. AI and ATS screening probability is high for the stated must-have requirements. A small keyword enhancement would be to use the exact phrase “HACCP knowledge” and, where accurate, “fresh meat for the service counter.” Avoid adding self-service packaging, tray-sealer, labelling-scale, or forklift terms because the candidate’s information does not support those claims.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV strongly matches the two must-have requirements: completed butcher training and substantially more than two years of meat-counter experience, plus documented HACCP practice. It aligns well with the role’s core duties through cutting, portioning, customer advice, FIFO rotation, and temperature recording. It also reflects the company’s emphasis on knowledgeable service, hygiene, fresh local meat, and practical experience. The candidate’s ongoing preparation for the Master Butcher exam is a positive development point and is accurately presented as preparation rather than a completed qualification. The candidate does not hold the nice-to-have forklift licence, which is a gap in the candidate’s background rather than a CV defect. The CV also does not demonstrate supermarket self-service packaging or tray-sealer experience; this is relevant context for the role but should not be presented as an achieved skill.
critique.improvement_instructions:

1. In the Professional Profile section, change the final phrase “and HACCP temperature checks” to “and HACCP knowledge, including temperature checks and FIFO stock rotation.” This uses the job description’s exact “HACCP knowledge” wording while remaining fully supported by the candidate’s experience.

2. In the Skills section, change “Cutting, portioning and preparing fresh meat for the counter” to “Cutting, portioning and preparing fresh meat for the service counter.” This more closely matches the advertisement’s terminology without claiming self-service packaging experience.

3. In the Butcher position at Mesnica Kod Ante, consider changing “bone, trim and portion meat for the counter” to “bone, trim and portion fresh meat for the service counter.” This improves keyword alignment and makes the relevance to the advertised counter duties immediately clear.
